title: JWT resource server rejects valid tokens with 'The iss claim is not valid': issuer-uri must match the token's iss including the trailing slash
errorSample:
java.lang.AssertionError: Status expected:<200> but was:<401>
    at org.springframework.test.util.AssertionErrors.fail(AssertionErrors.java:62)
    at org.springframework.test.util.AssertionErrors.assertEquals(AssertionErrors.java:129)
    at org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.StatusResultMatchers.lambda$matcher$0(StatusResultMatchers.java:600)
    at org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc$1.andExpect(MockMvc.java:212)
    at org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.StatusResultMatchersDsl.isOk(StatusResultMatchersDsl.kt:131)
symptom: Tokens with a correct signature get HTTP 401 and a WWW-Authenticate header saying 'The iss claim is not valid' when the resource server uses jwk-set-uri together with an issuer-uri property.
cause: JwtIssuerValidator compares the iss claim to issuer-uri as an exact string. Identity providers differ on whether the issuer URL ends with a slash, and the configured value does not match the token's iss claim, so every token is treated as having a foreign issuer.
fixSummary: Give the issuer-uri property a concrete default instead of an empty one: the issuer string that your identity provider puts in its tokens, with a trailing slash appended, for example spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri=${ISSUER_URI:<issuer string>/}. The exact string comparison then succeeds and valid tokens are accepted.
